assessments.reasoning: The survey design allows distinguishing de jure vs de facto female-headed households because marital status (Q209), presence/absence of partner (Q205, Q206), and incoming remittances/alimony (Q556) are collected individually for household members. Unpartnered mother-child units can be identified through Q203-A (Nº DE NÚCLEO FAMILIAR) and Q203-B (RELACIÓN DE PARENTESCO CON EL JEFE(A) DEL NÚCLEO FAMILIAR), which explicitly identify family sub-units within larger households alongside member sex and marital status. Women-maintained households or units can be identified through individual income collection for all members aged 14 and older in Module 500, enabling identification of the main economic provider regardless of who is recorded as household head. However, the instrument does not link mother-child sub-units to their own consumption, production, or care activities, as expenditure and consumption items (e.g. Q559, Q560) are recorded at the overall household level or per individual respondent, rather than mapped onto the family nucleus.
